items.meta_description: Choose what goes through the VPN and what connects directly, by country, domain, app, IP address or local network. Available in VpnHood!
items.title: Split tunneling
items.lead: Decide what goes through the VPN and what connects directly: by country, by domain, by app, by IP address, or by local network.
items.shot_alt: The Split tunneling screen in the VpnHood! app
items.platforms: Android, iOS, Windows and Linux. Splitting by app is available on Android only.
items.how_desc: Not everything benefits from a tunnel. Split tunneling routes chosen traffic outside the VPN, so a banking app keeps working, a local printer stays reachable, and bandwidth is not spent on traffic that never needed protecting.
items.when_desc: Use it when an app refuses to work over a VPN, when you want local devices like a TV or printer reachable, or when only some destinations need to be tunnelled.
items.cost_desc: Traffic you exclude is not protected by the VPN. That is the whole point, but it is worth being deliberate about what you leave outside.
items.kinds_desc: Each option has its own screen in the app and its own page here.
items.split_dns_desc: Decide whether DNS lookups follow your split rules or always stay inside the VPN.
items.by_app_short: Choose which apps use the VPN and which connect directly.
items.by_country_short: Route traffic through or around the VPN based on the country it is going to.
items.by_domain_short: Include, exclude, or block specific domains from VPN traffic.
items.by_ip_short: Decide which IP addresses use the VPN, on the device or inside the app, and what happens to IPv6.
items.local_network_short: Keep printers, TVs and other devices on your local network reachable while the VPN is on.
